People's Majlis Committee Minutes

12th meeting of the Environment and Climate Change Committee

11 August 2026

Venue of meeting: People's Majlis building (Committee Room 8)
Start time: 11:25

{Presiding: Chair of the Committee; Member for South Maafannu constituency, Abdulla Rifau}

Remarks from the Chair:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Welcome to the 12th meeting of the People's Majlis Environment and Climate Change Committee. The meeting is being held in Committee Room 8. Today's date is 12 August, Tuesday. The time is 11:25. Present at the committee at this time are myself (Member for South Maafannu constituency, Abdulla Rifau), Member for Mulaku constituency Ibrahim Naufal, Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa, Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla Shihab, Member for Keyodhoo constituency Mohamed Niushad, and Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig. On today's agenda is the review of the Bill to amend Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act). Accordingly, the bill's amendments are now displayed on the screen. I think that while we review it now, we should put up the other sheet with the comparison. That way the problem we ran into the other day will be resolved. Table. So, we will proceed with the following amendments to Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act). We sent this out for comment, and as of yesterday, when the comments were due, the reply was that no party had any comment. So, no relevant institution has any issue with this, nor any opinion on it. So, the law is in a state where we can look at whether there is anything further in it and conclude it very easily. The following amendments to Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act). 1- Amending Article 4(t) of the said Act as follows. To carry out all matters that the Authority is required to do under this Act, or under a special law relating to a public utility service, or under any other law, and to arrange other matters relating to the provision of public utility services in a manner consistent with this Act and the special laws relating to public utility services or other relevant laws. 2- Amending Article 6(b) of the said Act as follows. Article 6(b). The Board shall consist of 7 members, including the Chief Executive of the Authority, who is appointed to the Board by virtue of office. This, right, is the biggest change that has come in here. Previously 5

[stamp]

people. At that time the Chief Executive was not a board member either, right. 3- Amending the opening phrase of Article 7(a) of the said Act as follows. 7(a)- Excluding the Chief Executive of the Authority, those appointed to the Board as members of the Authority's Board of Directors shall be 1 member from each of the following fields, from among persons with technical education and experience in that field. Adding a number after number 5 of Article 7(a) of the said Act as follows. 7(a) 6- Legal field. This is the added [unclear] slot. 5- Amending Article 7(c) of the said Act as follows. Article 7(c). Excluding the Chief Executive of the Authority, each member appointed as a Board member under this Article shall be appointed for a term of 5 years. Adding a subsection after Article 7(c) of the said Act as follows. 7(d)- Notwithstanding what is stated in subsection (c) of this Article, every member other than members removed from Board membership under Article 9 of this Act may be appointed as a Board member for more than 1 term. Amending Article 8(a) of the said Act as follows. Article 8(a). The President shall appoint a member from among the Board members, excluding the Chief Executive of the Authority, to the post of Chairperson of the Board of Directors. 8- Amending Article 13(b) of the said Act as follows. Article 13(b). A Board meeting may be held only when a number of members equal to a majority of the total members of the Board, including the Chairperson of the Board, are present. Amending Article 13(d) of the said Act as follows. Article 13(d). If a number of members equal to a majority of the total members of the Board wish to hold a Board meeting, they may submit this to the Chairperson of the Board stating the reason. And the Chairperson of the Board shall hold a Board meeting in the manner proposed in that notice within five days of receiving the notice. 10- Amending a subsection after Article 13(e) of the said Act as follows. Sorry, adding a subsection. 13(f)- The Chief Executive shall not have the right to vote on any matter decided by the Board. 11- The member who must additionally be appointed to the Authority's Board of Directors in connection with the amendment made to Article 7(a) of the said Act by Article 4 of this Act shall be appointed within 30 days of this Act coming into force

[stamp]

shall be appointed. 12- This Act shall come into force on the day it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives.

Remarks from the Chair:
Member for North Hithadhoo constituency, Abdulla Sodig.

Remarks by Member for North Hithadhoo constituency, Abdulla Sodig:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. In number 10 here, 13(f) being added to Article 13: the Chief Executive shall not have the right to vote on any decision made by the Board. Now what has been added to the committee is the Chief Executive. Then in addition to that, a person for the legal field. With those added it becomes 7. The Chief Executive cannot vote. Then if everyone else can vote, in a situation where it comes to a vote, the vote is tied. Then how will it be decided? Isn't it 6 who are there to vote? The reason an odd number is usually brought into committees is so that a vote is not allowed to tie in any situation. Then in a very delicate situation, one person not voting and it then ending in a tie is a completely different matter. But even then the same problem will remain, right. 6 people vote. In a committee of 7 people the Chief Executive does not vote. What is the reason he does not vote? What is the reason he does not have to vote? Issues like this. Yes! Here, perhaps as you point out, the law says the Chief Executive is a person who must be accountable to this Board. Exempting the situations where he must be accountable may also be something that can be done. Otherwise, if the Chief Executive is put on the Board, isn't it done by making it 6 without adding another person? Now if the Chief Executive is to be kept on the Board, couldn't it be arranged with the same 5 people as before, without adding another person and without adding someone from the legal field? Even now, the Utility Regulatory Authority will have people in its legal department. The institution, the Authority, will employ someone to give it legal advice and do its legal work. I do not see any particular importance in having legal advice, a person from the legal field, on this Board. Then, if the purpose of the amendment now being proposed is to make the Chief Executive a board member, and if he does not vote, then by adding only him and making it 6, he would not vote and the remaining 5 members would vote, right.

[stamp]

So, the issue I face is that, as it is in the law here, the Chair also votes. It says everyone will vote. Then otherwise, what should be done is to make it so the Chair cannot vote. He would only have to vote in a tied situation. No, it says here that apart from him everyone votes.

Remarks from the Chair:
Member for West Maafannu constituency, Musthafa.

Remarks by Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim:
Thank you. What came to my mind is just as the Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig just put it: this general principle is actually that committees formed this way have 7 or 5 people and carry the work forward. In doing so, that principle is what has been set. If there are 7 people, there will be 6 people to vote. So, if the 6 people tie, if it is three against three, then the chair votes. This is actually the way it has been practised so far. And everywhere, in every way, what we see is it being practised this way. But looking at the change that has now been made to this law, we have always had in mind that there must be 7 people or 5 people. With that, when it ties, the chair votes and that decides it. But if it goes ahead with 6 people, 4 people, 8 people, there will be no chance of a tie [unclear]. There actually will be no chance of a tie [unclear], right. There will be no situation where, because there is a chance of a tie [unclear], the person presiding necessarily has to vote. So, if that practice can simply be changed in our minds, there will be no problem. Then the other way is that, whatever happens, even if we leave this law as it is, if the committee, or the principle and manner of running that committee, is planned so that the committee carries it forward, then in any case the chair here will just be a person who sits without voting. The chair will not be able to vote. Looking at the principle we usually practise, the chair here is actually not a person who votes, even if that opportunity exists. So, I just wanted to say that.

[stamp]

Remarks from the Chair:
Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa.

Remarks by Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim:
I then, well, I don't really think that is such a big issue, as it isn't that big an issue for me, and then a proposal has also been put forward. But as it is not getting support, it came to my mind to just say that no other party has sent us any comment on this. Since no further comment has come even from the public or from any party we sent it to, I think I will propose that the committee pass this bill as it is now, after correcting some spelling mistakes in it.

Remarks from the Chair:
Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed.

Remarks by Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. I second the proposal of the honourable Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa.

Remarks from the Chair:
Thank you. There is now a proposal, put forward by the Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim and seconded by the Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed, to pass the entire Bill to amend Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act), with any spelling mistakes in the bill corrected. So, I will put this proposal to a vote.

[stamp]

(Voting) Thank you. I announce that this has passed with the unanimous agreement of the members present at today's meeting. And for the purpose of the minutes, I will also read out the names of the members who joined after this meeting began: Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed, Member for South Thinadhoo constituency Mohamed Alsan, Member for Hithaadhoo constituency Mohamed Siruhaan. So, thank you very much. We will now close today's session. And for the members' information, I also want to say that tomorrow the report on the work we have done will be read out at the meeting of the Committee of the Whole House. Tomorrow there will be a Committee of the Whole House at 11 o'clock. At that committee we will be submitting the report on the work we last did. Thank you very much. Yes! I announce that we have closed today's session.

[stamp]
